html:
A raid on Conakry on 22 November 1970 by Portuguese troops and Guinean exiles from Portuguese Guinea, who came by sea to free Portuguese prisoners and to overthrow Sekou Toure.

Guinea was the main base of the PAIGC. The raiders freed 26 prisoners and burned PAIGC boats, but failed to find Amilcar Cabral or bring down the government, and withdrew. The UN Security Council condemned Portugal. Sekou Toure answered with mass arrests, show trials and public hangings, and thousands passed through Camp Boiro. See also the Guinea-Bissau War of Independence.
